Two of the five have changed since Monday. HubSpot changed how it charges for AI, and Salesforce added a new AI add-on price. I couldn't read HubSpot's pricing page live, so its current seat price is unconfirmed.

- **HubSpot: changed.** On Monday I said Starter was $20. A Nov 11 change log says HubSpot added "HubSpot Credits" for AI actions, with 500 included on Starter [R4]. Agent Builder was also added to the plans [R4]. A pilot in EMEA for new customers only replaces separate hubs with one seat plus credits [R6][R8]. A third-party site lists the Starter list price as $20, but it is not a live read [R7].
- **Pipedrive: unchanged as checked.** The live page shows $14 per seat per month, billed annually, on the entry plan [R3]. That plan is now called Lite, and I don't know when the name changed. Nova meeting intelligence is on every plan [R3].
- **Zoho CRM: unchanged as checked.** The live page showed no prices. A Nov 10 third-party page lists Standard at $14 per user per month, billed yearly [R14].
- **Salesforce: changed.** The live page still shows Pro Suite at $100 per user per month, billed annually [R29]. On Nov 10 Salesforce added Agentforce Coworker at a flat $50 per user per month [R19]. It also plans to charge for external AI-agent API and MCP calls against Flex Credits, with the cost not yet specified [R22].
- **Close: unchanged as checked.** The live page shows Solo at $9, billed annually, but it is limited to 1 user [R1]. For your 20-person team the relevant entry plan is Essentials at $35 [R1]. The only new item I found is a minor one: a tone while outbound calls connect [R24].

Checked: I read the live pricing pages for Pipedrive, Zoho, Salesforce and Close. The HubSpot page failed to load. I ran one news search per vendor from Nov 9. I found no change for Pipedrive, Zoho or Close in what I checked.

**On 3 November you asked: "Which managed Postgres host has the cheapest entry paid plan?" My answer then was partly wrong, and it is still wrong today.** Neon Launch has no $5/month plan, and that was my error. Render Postgres at $6/month is the cheapest entry paid plan of the three.

- **Neon:** I said Launch "starts at $5/month". Neon's pricing page now shows Launch as pay-as-you-go with no monthly minimum, at $0.106 per CU-hour plus $0.35 per GB-month of storage [R1]. Verdict: **changed**. I can't tell whether it was ever a flat $5. Neon's own page puts a small database at about $15/month [R1].
- **Supabase:** I said Pro is $25/month. Pro is still "from $25/month" [R7]. Verdict: **unchanged as checked**.
- **Render:** I said Postgres starts at $6/month. The smallest paid instance is still $6/month, with storage at $0.30/GB [R18]. Verdict: **unchanged as checked**.

Each figure is a monthly price, but they are billed differently. Neon is usage-based, Supabase is a flat plan fee, and Render is a flat price per instance plus storage. The Render $6 instance has only 256 MB of RAM [R18].

Checked: I read the live pricing pages for Neon, Supabase and Render. I also searched news for each, dated from 3 Nov. The Neon news I found was about the Free plan and AI Gateway [R13], not Launch pricing. I found no pricing change at Supabase or Render in what I checked.

Render Postgres' entry paid instance is $6/month, which is about ₹562/month. Render's page lists the price in USD only [R1]. I didn't find any INR pricing from Render.

- **Earlier answer (2026-11-11):** I said the smallest paid instance was $6/month for compute, with storage extra. Render's pricing page, read live now, still shows that (0.1 CPU, 256 MB RAM) at $6/month, plus $0.30/GB for expandable storage [R1]. Verdict: unchanged as checked.
- **INR conversion:** The rupee closed provisionally at 93.70 per US dollar today [R6]. I calculated ₹562 as $6 × 93.70, and storage as roughly ₹28/GB (0.30 × 93.70). Other sources show rates between 93.66 and 93.76, so the result barely moves [R3][R4].

This is the mid-market rate. Your card or bank will likely add a markup, and any GST or taxes aren't included. I didn't check whether Render charges Indian customers in USD.
